title: Quantum oscillations in proximity to high-angular-momentum band inversion
abstract: Quantum oscillations provide a fundamental probe of electronic structure in magnetic fields, revealing the Fermi surface topology in metals, and/or the quasiparticle properties even in the insulating regimes. Here we study quantum oscillations in minimal models of high-angular-momentum (HAM) band inversion for both a chiral two-band model and a time-reversal-invariant four-band model. In the former case, finite oscillations can appear at the hybridized Chern-insulating regime due to thermal-activated excitations. In the latter case, interference between the two time-reversal-related blocks drives a strong deviation from the Lifshitz-Kosevich form, producing a non-monotonic temperature dependence of the oscillation amplitude and characteristic suppression temperatures whose number follows the angular momentum $l$. These results identify experimentally accessible signatures of HAM band inversion and provide a framework for other discrete-symmetry-related hybridizations and excitonic pairings.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes quantum oscillations near high-angular-momentum band inversion using minimal two-band and four-band models. The key finding is that the interference between time-reversal partners causes deviations from standard theory, producing unique temperature-dependent suppression signatures whose number directly tracks the angular momentum $l$. This offers an experimentally accessible fingerprint for characterizing such topological electronic states.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum oscillations (QOs) in electronic systems exhibiting High-Angular-Momentum (HAM) band inversion, particularly focusing on regimes beyond standard metallic Fermi surface quantization.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that HAM band inversion leads to characteristic deviations from the Lifshitz-Kosevich form, manifesting as non-monotonic temperature dependence and suppression temperatures whose number scales with the angular momentum $l$.
method: Theoretical analysis involves calculating the oscillatory density of states (LEDOS) using semiclassical quantization rules derived from generalized two-band and four-band Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The models include a minimal chiral two-band Hamiltonian and an extended time-reversal invariant four-band model, designed to capture topological transitions associated with band inversion ($\delta\mu$).
key_observables: Quantum oscillation amplitude, frequency ($F_0$), temperature dependence of the LEDOS, and characteristic suppression temperatures ($T_c$).
important_parameters: Angular momentum $l$, detuning parameter $\delta\mu$ (controlling inversion), magnetic field $B$, and temperature $T$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on semiclassical quantization rules for both metallic (Fermi surface crossing) and insulating (band-edge averaging) regimes, and assumes the applicability of thermal averaging kernels.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures showing inversion transitions, Landau level spectra ($E_{1,2}^n$ vs $1/B$), and crucially, detrended LEDOS oscillations confirming spectral weight suppression at characteristic temperatures whose count follows $l$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the two-band model in the insulating regime, then extending to a four-band time-reversal symmetric system. The core development involves deriving the total oscillatory LEDOS via interference between time-reversal partners, leading to the identification of $l$-dependent signatures.
why_interesting: The focus on temperature-dependent interference effects and the explicit link between oscillation features (suppression temperatures) and a geometric parameter ($l$) provides a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool for exotic topological phases in condensed matter systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. HAM band inversion. (a) Trivial band insulator with δµ < 0. (b) Quadratic band touching at δµ = 0. (c) Chern insulator with δµ > 0. Here, Chern number C = 2 for l = 2, and the Berry phase Φ(k) is plotted with Φ(kF ) = 2π. The same structure extends to l ≥2, where the inverted insula- tor has the Chern number C = l. (d) Hybridized dispersions E1,2(k) for l = 1, 2, 3 with different hybridizations V . “kF ” denotes the crossing point of the unhybridized bands and is measured in inverse-length units.

FIG. 2. Landau-level spectrum E1,2 n . (a,b) For δµ ≤0, the LLs are monotonic in 1/B, and the system remains (almost) insulating. (c) For δµ > 0, the LLs are non-monotonic in 1/B, and the system cross overs from metallic-like to insulating behavior as 1/B increases. The orange dashed curve shows the corresponding unhybridized LLs for comparison.

FIG. 3. Quantum oscillations of the LEDOS for the two-band model with l = 2. The oscillation behaviors for different detunings and temperatures are shown in (a) and (b), respectively.
